recipes.name: Pressure Cooker Mashed Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 3 cups cold water, or as needed
3.5 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and sliced 3/4 inch thick

steps.text: Bring water to a boil in a pressure cooker over high heat. When water is boiling, add potatoes. Seal lid and bring cooker up to high pressure. Reduce heat to low, maintaining high pressure, and cook for 15 to 30 minutes.

Use quick-release method to lower the pressure. Drain potatoes and return them to pressure cooker. Add butter and milk and cover pressure cooker with lid for 5 minutes, allowing the heat from the potatoes to melt the butter and warm the milk.
Remove lid. Season with kosher salt and white pepper, and use a hand masher to mash potatoes until lumps are mostly gone. Transfer to a bowl and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Pressure Cooker Mashed Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These fluffy mashed potatoes made in the pressure cooker with butter and milk are seasoned perfectly for a rich and comforting side dish.

review.reviewBody: Makes perfect mashed potatoes. I have a cuisinart electric pressure cooker and it only takes 5 minutes on high pressure to get the potatoes soft. I used half the salt, a little more cream, and no pepper. Excellent recipe!

A good basic recipe, flavor-wise, but the cook time is WAY off. I used an electric pressure cooker (which cooks slightly slower than the stove-top pressure cooker used in this recipe) and assuming you use potatoes cut to the stated 3/4"size, it takes 8-10 minutes, MAX. They wouldn't even take 30 mins if you were to boil them in a pot on the stove! I did add a bit more milk, personal preference, and I also like the recipe creator's suggestion to add horseradish. Mashing them by hand (as in the recipe) is far superior to using a mixer to avoid gluey potatoes.

This recipe is great but I can't imagine what 30 minutes of cooking time would do. That is crazy! I just made this ith a stove top pressure cooker, . I set the timer for 5 minutes when the steam was flowing steadily. I did the rapid release to reduce pressure. I think I cooked it for at least one minute too long (if not more). After draining the potatoes, I had to stir back into the hot pot to get the liquid (from overcooking) to evaporate before I could finish the recipe. Maybe 30 is a typo! I bet 3 minutes is right.

I have to adjust for my own cooker...they were a bit soupy but GOOD. Less water next time or more potatoes and only 8 minutes in my Gourmia Pressure Cooker. Thank You for this recipe. A favorite for sure.

Agree with Dale and Alice. Thirty minutes was way too long for my pressure cooker. Tried 15 minutes and will go down to 12 for next round. However, I must say, that even at 15 minutes, these were the best mashed potatoes I ever had. I used a can of chicken broth in the bottom of the cooker. Delish and so easy to mash with a fork! Will keep trying until I get time exactly right.

This is an addition to my previous review. After these were made in my instant pot, I sprinkled some fresh chives on top, put the lid back on and locked it and set it to “warm” because my dinner was delayed by 90 minutes! They were hot and fluffy and beautiful when I opened the lid!

These are SO good! This was my first time making non-instant potatoes (at 50 y/o!!), so I was nervous! I used chicken broth instead of water as some recommended. I also used half and half bc I didn't have whole milk. Lastly, I added some chives Philadelphia cream cheese (about 4 oz) and I'm telling you, I will never use instant potatoes again! Thank you!
Good recipe, but for my Fissler pressure cooker, cook time is way too long. I shortened to 15 min and it was plenty long. Will try 5 minutes next time and see how that goes.

I cooked 5# of peeled potatoes for 5 minutes in my pressure cooker, and they were perfectly done. I then drained them and followed one of the crockpot mashed pota to recipes. They were very good and hot for our Thanksgiving meal.

I've been pressure cooking for over 50 years and I usually pressure cook potatoes anywhere from 10-15 minutes at the most. 30 minutes is a long time. You're right, the trick is to use warm milk and butter, makes a huge difference. I think people that use a hand mixer prefer very creamy potatoes. I prefer a potato masher myself, but that's personal preference.

I was a bit rushed when I made these in my Instant Pot. I brought the water to a simmer, rather than a full boil, before adding potatoes and cooked at high pressure for 4 minutes. I had to do a 10 minute natural release instead of a quick release because some of the water started to come out when I tried the quick release. I just waited about 10 minutes and then released the rest of the pressure. Nice fluffy potatoes! Thanks for a great recipe! :)
No complaints from family or kids. My go to method over stovetop.
I also threw in just a little cream cheese as well.
I used the recipe, as is. Delicious. I love potatoes, no matter how they are fixed, but mashed are my favorite kind of potato. And this recipe is so hood and easy.
Turned out perfect!
30 MINUTES MY POTATOES WERE MUCH. THE 8 MINUTE ON HIGH WORKS PERFECT. THIS SUCKED, TRIED TO SALVAGE THEM BY ADDING 3 MORE POTATOES...DIDN'T WORK.
Super easy and came out perfect even though i left potatoes in pressure cooker for a really long time.

I am not sure if my pressure cooker is different but 30 minutes would cook 3/4" sliced potatoes into oblivion in my cooker... 15 minutes would be more than long enough... I normally quarter my potatoes and they cook through in less than 10 minutes. I'm at high altitude which may make a small difference!
So easy! I did add 5 large cloves of garlic when I added the milk and butter.
These worked beautifully! Fluffy buttery, and delicious! I can see adding in some other things to take it to another level, but for mashed potatoes; as is AWESOME! I love them!
